title: GlobalFoundries to Invest $10 Million in Cyient Semiconductors at $490 Million Valuation
excerpt: The strategic stake in the Hyderabad chip-design company matches the price of its recent Edelweiss-led round and takes its combined post-money valuation to $510 million.
body:
• Cyient Semiconductors has approved a $10 million strategic equity investment from GlobalFoundries, the company announced on Thursday, November 19.
  • The deal is priced at a $490 million pre-money equity valuation, the same as the Hyderabad company's recent Edelweiss-led financing round, taking its combined post-money valuation to $510 million.
  • GlobalFoundries U.S. Inc. will subscribe to compulsorily convertible preference shares. The investment has been approved; it completes under a shareholders' agreement and has not yet closed.
  • Cyient says the backing will expand its turnkey custom ASIC business, speed up custom silicon development and secure long-term wafer supply.

GlobalFoundries will invest $10 million in Cyient Semiconductors as a strategic investor, the Hyderabad-based custom silicon company announced on Thursday. The investment will be made at a pre-money equity valuation of $490 million — the same valuation as Cyient Semiconductors' recent financing round led by Edelweiss — and together the two transactions take the company's post-money equity valuation to $510 million, according to the company's statement, reported by The Hindu BusinessLine.

How the deal is structured

Cyient Semiconductors is the chip design arm of Cyient Ltd, the Hyderabad engineering services group. Under the transaction disclosed to stock exchanges, GlobalFoundries U.S. Inc. will subscribe to fully and compulsorily convertible cumulative preference shares of Cyient Semiconductors for the rupee equivalent of $10 million. The shareholders' agreement takes effect on completion of the investment, so the transaction announced this week is an approved deal rather than a closed one. The Edelweiss round it is priced against was led by EAAA India Alternatives Ltd, formerly Edelweiss Alternative Asset Advisors.

The stake is small in percentage terms — $10 million against a $510 million post-money valuation — but strategic in kind: GlobalFoundries is one of the world's largest contract chip manufacturers, and the investment makes a foundry partner a shareholder in a design company that depends on foundries to turn its designs into silicon.

What the money is for

Cyient Semiconductors said the investment will be used to expand its turnkey custom ASIC (application-specific integrated circuit) business, accelerate custom silicon development and strengthen long-term wafer supply assurance and supply chain resilience. The company designs chips for customers in the automotive, industrial, AI, communications and data centre markets, and runs design centres in India, Belgium and the United States.

"Having a leading semiconductor ecosystem partner as a strategic investor validates our technology and business model, accelerates our access to advanced manufacturing capabilities, and strengthens our ability to deliver custom silicon and power products globally."

— Suman Narayan, CEO, Cyient Semiconductors

Narayan said India has the talent and technical depth to become a significant force in the global semiconductor industry, and that the company's ambition is to develop differentiated custom silicon from India for global markets, according to the company's announcement.

What to watch

The next marker is completion: the shareholders' agreement becomes effective when the investment closes, and the filing does not set a date for that. For the parent group, the deal also marks a step in Cyient Semiconductors' emergence as a separately valued business — the Edelweiss round and now GlobalFoundries' entry price the standalone chip unit at $510 million post-money, a figure investors can now track against Cyient Ltd's own market value.
